examples.trans: Would I really break a friend's finger for free?

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно.
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free.

examples.text: Дети проходят бесплатно.
examples.trans: Children get in free.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to break', paired with 'сломать'.

examples.text: Шеф, вы не хотите мне палец сломать?
examples.trans: Chef, would you like to break my finger?

examples.text: Не будешь работать, я тебе спину сломаю!
examples.trans: If you do not work, I will break your back!

examples.text: Если палец будет сломан, я получу деньги.
examples.trans: If my finger is broken, I will get money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А сегодня последний день этой моей страховки.
examples.trans: And today is the very last day of this insurance of mine.

examples.text: По-моему, это просто отличный и выгодный бизнес.
examples.trans: In my opinion, it is simply great and profitable business.

examples.text: А что это за особый случай сегодня?
examples.trans: And what is this special occasion today?

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will give', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.text: Деньги за зеркало я тебе потом отдам.
examples.trans: I will pay you back for the mirror later.

examples.text: То есть я отдам деньги и выйду в ноль?
examples.trans: So I give you the money and break even?

examples.text: Ну что, доченька, ты уже отдала заказ?
examples.trans: Well, sweetheart, did you already deliver the order?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А на следующий день он страховку оформил.
examples.trans: And the very next day he took out an insurance policy.

examples.text: А сегодня последний день этой моей страховки.
examples.trans: And today is the very last day of this insurance of mine.

examples.text: Если палец будет сломан, я получу деньги.
examples.trans: If my finger is broken, I will get money.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'I'll get out', paired with 'выходить'.

related.gloss: not to I'll get out (negated infinitive)

examples.text: То есть я отдам деньги и выйду в ноль?
examples.trans: So I give you the money and break even?

examples.text: Мне нужны деньги на мой новый фильм.
examples.trans: I need money for my new movie.

examples.text: Скажите, новый страховой полис оформлять будем?
examples.trans: Tell me, shall we sign you up for a new insurance policy?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сеня, ты чего там вдруг завис?
examples.trans: Senya, why did you freeze up over there?

examples.text: Шеф, вы не хотите мне палец сломать?
examples.trans: Chef, would you like to break my finger?

examples.text: А на следующий день он страховку оформил.
examples.trans: And the very next day he took out an insurance policy.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'zero; nil' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: То есть я отдам деньги и выйду в ноль?
examples.trans: So I give you the money and break even?

examples.text: Всё, у меня денег совсем в ноль.
examples.trans: That's it, my money is completely down to zero.

examples.text: Самсон, ты ведь тоже уже в ноль.
examples.trans: Samson, you are also already at zero after all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не будешь работать, я тебе спину сломаю!
examples.trans: If you do not work, I will break your back!

examples.text: Хотите скинуться на подарок вместе с нами?
examples.trans: Would you like to chip in for the gift with us?

examples.text: Ты мне нужен на час или два.
examples.trans: I need you for an hour or two.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я четыре года назад порезал себе палец.
examples.trans: Four years ago I cut my finger.

examples.text: И за четыре года нет ни одной царапины.
examples.trans: And in four years he has not had a single scratch.

examples.text: Да ты лучше себе сразу голову сломай!
examples.trans: You might as well break your own head right away!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'specifically', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну да, именно так я и предлагаю.
examples.trans: Well yes, that is exactly what I am proposing.

examples.text: Чего мы стоим, давайте поздравлять именинницу!
examples.trans: Why are we standing around, let us congratulate the birthday girl!

examples.text: Ну и что же именно он такое говорит?
examples.trans: Well and what exactly is it saying?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну да, именно так я и предлагаю.
examples.trans: Well yes, that is exactly what I am proposing.

examples.text: Иди ты в баню с такой помощью!
examples.trans: Get lost with that kind of help!

examples.text: Ведь он тебе всё-таки родной отец.
examples.trans: After all, he is still your own father.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'лагать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning '(I) suggest', paired with 'предложить'.

examples.text: Ну да, именно так я и предлагаю.
examples.trans: Well yes, that is exactly what I am proposing.

examples.text: Что вы предлагаете?
examples.trans: What do you suggest?

examples.text: Он предлагает работу.
examples.trans: He is offering a job.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Костик, не злись, ему некуда было идти.
examples.trans: Kostik, do not be angry, he had nowhere else to go.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'bathhouse' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Иди ты в баню с такой помощью!
examples.trans: Get lost with that kind of help!

examples.text: Теперь разрешите пригласить вас в баню.
examples.trans: Now allow me to invite you to the bathhouse.

examples.text: Это настоящая хорошая русская баня.
examples.trans: It is a genuine, good Russian bathhouse.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, what sort', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну да, именно так я и предлагаю.
examples.trans: Well yes, that is exactly what I am proposing.

examples.text: Иди ты в баню с такой помощью!
examples.trans: Get lost with that kind of help!

examples.text: Ведь он тебе всё-таки родной отец.
examples.trans: After all, he is still your own father.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хватит смеяться, лучше бы ты мне помог!
examples.trans: Stop laughing, you had better help me instead!

examples.text: Иди ты в баню с такой помощью!
examples.trans: Get lost with that kind of help!

examples.text: Помогите, он меня сейчас задушит!
examples.trans: Help, he is going to strangle me right now!

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'йтись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'it will be necessary', paired with 'приходиться'.

examples.text: Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.

examples.text: Нам пришлось долго ждать.
examples.trans: We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'gift, present' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Надо срочно найти хороший подарок!
examples.trans: I must urgently find a good gift!

examples.text: Хотите скинуться на подарок вместе с нами?
examples.trans: Would you like to chip in for the gift with us?

examples.text: Это отличный подарок от родного отца!
examples.trans: That is an excellent gift from her own father!

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to invent', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.text: Придётся мне самому подарок придумать.
examples.trans: I will have to think up a gift myself.

examples.text: Ты сам это придумал!
examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Я придумаю план.
examples.trans: I'll think up a plan.
